organization.name: Tanzania Health Alliance
organization.mission: To advance public health through advocacy, capacity building, research, and partnerships, contributing to sustainable and resilient healthcare in Tanzania.
organization.vision: To achieve a healthier Tanzania where every individual has access to equitable and quality healthcare.

home.heroDescription: We address critical public health challenges including Viral Hepatitis, HIV, and Mental Health through awareness, advocacy, and improved access to care across Tanzania.

home.engagementTitle: Turning advocacy into conversations that can move policy

about.heroText: Tanzania Health Alliance (THA) is a registered NGO (No. 00NGO/R/8379) based in Dar es Salaam. We work with communities, health institutions and partners on Viral Hepatitis, HIV and Mental Health.
about.founderStory: The organization was inspired by the personal experience of its founder, Shaibu Issa, who lost his brother to liver cancer in 2021, a preventable condition with early detection and vaccination. This experience led to the creation of THA to increase awareness, promote prevention, improve access to healthcare, and address stigma related to diseases such as hepatitis.
about.campaignsIntro: Our work is organized through focused campaigns so that activities, partners and results can be traced back to a clear public-health purpose.
about.partnersIntro: Working with organizations that strengthen our reach, technical work and accountability.
about.closingText: If our work aligns with your institution, community or funding priorities, we would be glad to start with a practical conversation about where collaboration can make the most difference.

funding.heroText: Work with us where your time, funding or institutional support can meet a clear public-health need.
funding.donationIntro: We welcome support for clearly defined activities, with an agreed purpose, budget and reporting approach.
funding.institutionalText: For institutional or project funding, THA can agree the activity, target group, budget, timeline and reporting requirements before implementation begins.
funding.partnerIntro: If our work aligns with your organization, tell us what you are trying to achieve and where collaboration may make sense.

coreValues.description: We act with honesty, transparency and accountability.
We work so quality health information and services are easier to reach, regardless of background or location.
We work with communities, institutions and partners because public-health problems are rarely solved by one organization alone.
We prefer documented work, measurable results and credible health guidance over broad claims.

academy.heroText: Find clear answers about HIV, viral hepatitis and mental health, then explore trusted guidance when you want to learn more.

guides.title: HIV can be prevented and treated
guides.summary: Testing is the only way to know your HIV status. Early treatment protects your health, and people who take effective treatment can live long, healthy lives.

guides.title: Protect your liver from viral hepatitis
guides.summary: Hepatitis B and C can damage the liver without obvious early symptoms. Vaccination prevents hepatitis B, while testing and treatment help prevent serious complications.

guides.title: Mental health deserves care
guides.summary: Persistent sadness, anxiety, sleep problems or loss of interest can affect anyone. Speaking with someone you trust and seeking professional support are important first steps.

helpText: Visit a health facility if you may have been exposed to HIV or hepatitis, need testing, or have symptoms that concern you. Early advice and treatment can make a major difference.
If emotional distress is affecting daily life, speak with a qualified health professional or someone you trust. Urgent help is important if you or another person may be in immediate danger.
These resources support learning and informed conversations; a health professional can provide advice for your individual needs.

hepatitis.title: Viral Hepatitis in Tanzania
hepatitis.intro: Tanzania Health Alliance works to improve awareness, prevention, early testing, vaccination advocacy and access to care for viral hepatitis, with particular attention to hepatitis B.
hepatitis.overview: Viral hepatitis can damage the liver for years before symptoms become obvious. Earlier testing, prevention and linkage to care can reduce avoidable illness and deaths.
hepatitis.whyItMatters: Hepatitis B can be prevented through vaccination, while testing helps people understand their status and seek appropriate care.
actions: Advocacy for hepatitis B vaccination, including the birth dose
Promoting testing and linkage to appropriate care
Working with health and policy stakeholders

hiv.title: HIV Awareness and Community Health in Tanzania
hiv.intro: Tanzania Health Alliance supports HIV awareness, stigma reduction, testing education, treatment access and community-led health engagement in Tanzania.
hiv.overview: HIV prevention, testing and treatment have changed what is possible for people living with HIV, but stigma and gaps in access still prevent some people from getting help early.
hiv.whyItMatters: Knowing your status and starting appropriate treatment early protects health and supports better long-term outcomes.
actions: Partnership and advocacy around access to care

mental-health.title: Mental Health Awareness in Tanzania
mental-health.intro: Tanzania Health Alliance supports mental health awareness, stigma reduction, youth resilience, peer support and healthier community conversations in Tanzania.
mental-health.overview: Mental-health challenges can affect study, work, relationships and physical health. Young people may face particular pressure during school-to-work and other major life transitions.
mental-health.whyItMatters: Early support, safe conversations and access to qualified care can help people manage distress before it becomes more severe.
actions: Referral to appropriate professional support where needed

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: How Tanzania Health Alliance handles information shared through this website.

sections.heading: Information we collect
sections.text: We collect information that you voluntarily provide through contact, registration, partnership, volunteer, donation and administrative forms. We may also collect limited technical information needed to keep the website secure and reliable.

sections.heading: How information is used
sections.text: Information is used to respond to requests, manage participation in THA activities, operate the website, protect accounts and improve our public-health programmes and communications.

sections.heading: Information sharing
sections.text: THA does not sell personal information. Information is shared only with authorised service providers or partners when necessary to deliver a requested service, comply with the law or protect people and the organisation.

sections.heading: Your choices
sections.text: You may request access, correction or deletion of information you submitted by contacting THA. Some records may be retained when required for security, legal or programme-accountability purposes.

cookies.title: Cookies Policy
cookies.intro: How this website uses essential browser storage and similar technologies.

sections.heading: Essential storage
sections.text: The website may use essential cookies or browser storage to maintain secure administrator sessions, remember necessary preferences and protect forms.

sections.heading: Analytics
sections.text: If audience measurement is enabled, it should be configured to collect only the information needed to understand website performance and improve public information.

sections.heading: Your control
sections.text: You can remove or block cookies through your browser settings. Blocking essential storage may prevent secure areas of the website from working correctly.

terms.title: Terms and Conditions
terms.intro: Conditions for using Tanzania Health Alliance’s public website and information.

sections.heading: Health information
sections.text: Website content is provided for education and public awareness. It does not replace diagnosis, treatment or advice from a qualified health professional. Seek urgent medical help when needed.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
sections.text: Do not misuse the website, attempt unauthorised access, interfere with its operation or submit unlawful, harmful or misleading material.

sections.heading: Content and links
sections.text: THA works to keep information accurate and current. External links are provided for context and remain the responsibility of their respective publishers.

sections.heading: Updates
sections.text: These terms may be updated when website services or legal requirements change. The current version will remain available on this page.
